reviews.title: Ruined by Forced AI Anti-Features
reviews.text:
I was a late adopter of WhatsApp due to its association with Facebook (now Meta). I was surprised at how conservatively it was managed over the years; new features were added slowly and were mostly unintrusive. This changed in 2025 when Meta started introducing AI to the platform, leveraging various dark patterns to encourage users to engage with Meta’s new AI-powered search and summary anti-features.

In the most recent update, there is now an icon for another AI that Meta has branded as Muse. Further, the “Star” “Pin” and “Info” options that used to appear when a user long-pressed a comment are now hidden behind a “More…” button, with the original features now being replaced with a “Ask Meta AI” button. There is no option to remove this anti-feature.

Cynically, I can’t help but think that the placement of this button was intended to cause users to press the button accidentally, breaking the encryption Meta ostensibly provides in order to supply the company with private messages to be used as training data. Meta’s continued insistence on forcing these anti-features into the app have caused me to begin looking into alternative platforms.

reviews.title: App Lock on WhatsApp Web/Desktop Doesn't Hide Chats — Please Fix
reviews.text: I'm writing to report a serious privacy issue with the App Lock feature on WhatsApp for laptop/desktop (WhatsApp Web and the desktop app). When I enable App Lock under Privacy settings, I expect it to fully lock the app so that nobody else can see my chats. Instead, it only prevents others from sending messages — my entire chat list and message history remain fully visible to anyone who opens the app on my laptop. Anyone can pick up my laptop, open WhatsApp, and read all my private conversations. This defeats the entire purpose of a lock. If the feature is called "App Lock," it should: 1. Require my password, PIN, or biometric authentication before showing any content — including the chat list, message previews, and individual conversations. 2. Completely hide/blur all chats until I unlock the app. 3. Lock automatically after a set period of inactivity or when the screen locks. Please make App Lock on WhatsApp Web/Desktop work like a true privacy lock — the same way it works on the mobile app — so that no one can see my messages without my permission. Privacy is the whole point of this feature, and right now it doesn't deliver that on laptop. Thank you.

That said, if you still need a cross-platform non native solution you’re far better off using the original Signal app, before they licensed their software to Meta so WhatsApp could track everyone you connect with and amalgamate all that data with everything else they collect on you across all their services and your traffic and habits all over the internet outside their services.

On an aesthetic level, this app is kind of ugly. It’s been a year since ios26 was announced and they have yet to adopt any of the new look or clean up their outdated interface.

reviews.title: WhatsApp on Apple Watch without standalone support
reviews.text:
Having WhatsApp on Apple Watch without true standalone functionality makes very little sense.

If a cellular Apple Watch already has its own network connection and internet access, requiring the iPhone to remain nearby defeats the purpose entirely. The watch can already handle calls and data on its own, so WhatsApp should be able to send and receive messages independently as well.

A lot of users buy a cellular Apple Watch specifically so they can leave the phone behind during workouts, walks, or short trips. In its current state, the experience feels unnecessarily limited and incomplete.

Please add full standalone support for Apple Watch cellular models.

reviews.title: Customer Support is All AI - Incredibly Frustrating

However, each time I sent a chat, I was restricted from using WhatsApp within the hour. This was very frustrating for me because I reviewed the terms of use and did nothing to violate them. I appealed for a review each time and was able to get back in to my account, but it was only a matter of time before I was restricted again. I had WhatsApp for about 5 days before it banned my account fully, which I knew did not make sense because I had done nothing worth being banned. When I reached out to customer support for help, they sent me back the same AI message each time and would not escalate the issue to a human. I understand that systems have flaws and AI is not perfected, but I am very frustrated with how WhatsApp’s customer support is designed. I do not want to leave a poor review because I was enjoying using WhatsApp for the short time I had it, but I believe everyone should be made aware of this problem, and I hope the developer will see my message and work to fix the system.
